newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Re sees '97 results helped by start.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Re sees '97 results helped by start.

text.p: Swiss Reinsurance Co said it expected 1997 results to benefit from a good start, an improved balance sheet structure and a wider consolidation after acquisitions last year.

"The overall favourable course of business at the start of the year, an improved balance sheet structure and the expansion of consolidation will have a beneficial effect on annual results," Swiss Re said in a letter to shareholders.
Swiss Re said its technical risk position was improved by its biggest acquisition last year, the purchase of British life and health reinsurer Mercantile & General Re.
"The growth in life business has a stabilising effect on profit quality," Swiss Re said.
"Financial markets have developed very well since the start of this year but are at the moment in a unsettled phase," said the reinsurer, whose huge assets make it a major investor.
Swiss Re on Friday reported that 1996 net profit jumped 33 percent to 1.459 billion Swiss francs after minorities, overshooting market expectations, partly due to a much higher investment return.

Swiss Re said business would also expand this year due to the first-time consolidation of Mercantile & General and the remaining 51 percent of Unione Italiana di Riassicurazione (Uniorias) it agreed to buy in April.
Swiss Re said this year's results will also include a higher stake in Bermuda-based Partner Re, where it plans to raise its holding from 11.1 percent to 21.8 percent.

Swiss Re set its annual shareholder meeting for June 27 starting at 9:30 a.m. (0730 GMT) in Zurich. It said on Friday the baord was proposing a higher dividend of 30 swiss francs per share after 22.50 the year before.
